prompts: The game went down in June and we owe the team an incident report. The logs and their notes are in {WS}/logs. When did it start and end, how long was it, did we keep our monthly availability target, and why did it happen? Record it in {WS}/result.json: start, end, minutes_down, availability_june_pct, slo_999_ok, root_cause.
answers:
Done. [goal] Incident report for the June game-server outage in ./result.json. [action] Read logs/README.md (SLO 99.9%, June = 30 days, one incident; down = first save error → "server ready"), grepped all three daily logs for error/ready markers, read the full incident section, and computed the numbers with a PowerShell script. [result] result.json written:

- start: 2026-06-02 03:17:42 (first `ERROR SaveGame failed: write /data/game/Saved/Level.sav: No space left on device`)
- end: 2026-06-02 03:53:31 (`INFO server ready, accepting players`)
- minutes_down: 35.8167 (2149 s)
- availability_june_pct: 99.9171 = (2592000 − 2149) / 2592000 × 100
- slo_999_ok: true (99.9171 ≥ 99.9, marginally)
- root_cause: /data disk full (WARN at 03:10:02, 97% usage) → save writes failed with ENOSPC → server unresponsive, watchdog crash loop (exit 137) until backup rotation freed 38.2 GB at 03:52:10.

How I know it's right: the down window follows the README's own definition (first save error to "server ready"); grep confirmed these are the only save errors and the only "server ready" line across all three logs; the 06-01 RCON auth failure is noise, not a save error; the arithmetic was run in a script, not by hand. Assumptions: "first save error" = the 06-02 03:17:42 ENOSPC error (the 03:10 disk WARN is a warning, not a save error); June counted as a full 30-day month per the README. No browser tabs or apps were opened, so nothing to close.
